internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every occurrence of this root in the Quran is packed into two adjacent verses (17:26–27) and every one is Form II: the prohibited verb 'do not squander' (تُبَذِّر), its own emphatic cognate object 'a squandering' (تَبْذِيرًا), and the name for the people who do it, 'the squanderers' (المُبَذِّرِين). The verse first commands giving the kinsman, the needy, and the wayfarer their due (حَقّ), then forbids تبذير in the same breath — so the root does NOT mean giving/spending as such (that is carried by ءَاتِ, root أ ت ي); it marks a condemned, wrongful outflow that overshoots or misses the rightful due. The next verse grounds its wrongness theologically: the squanderers are 'brothers of the devils,' and the devil is 'ungrateful (كَفُور) to his Lord.' Because all three tokens are one lexeme in one micro-context, we can confidently say WHAT the class means here, but we cannot separate a deep root nucleus from this single Form-II lexicalization, and we cannot decide whether the fault is quantitative (excess) or directional (misdirected).
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: NOT rightful giving/generosity (إِيتَاء of the حَقّ is commanded in the same verse; the root names only its censured breach). NOT hoarding/withholding (the frame is one of releasing wealth, not retaining it). NOT a neutral or agricultural 'scatter/sow seed' sense (zero Quran-internal attestation; importing it would be a barred external lexical prior). NOT demonstrably a pure quantity/abundance term (the censure is moral — brotherhood of devils, ingratitude — not merely 'a lot'). NOT demonstrably synonymous with إسراف (s-r-f) or any other 'waste/extravagance' root (no neighbour root occurs in this packet; synonymy is untestable and neither asserted nor denied). NOT licensed to generalize to a bare-root (Form I) meaning — Form I is unattested.
